newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 19.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Lifting the last of the state's restrictions on the movement of foreign capital is now a priority for the Bank of Greece, which is reported to be ready to announce new guidelines within the first 10 days of June. Apart from the complete deregulation of deposits in foreign exchange, among the measures to be abolished is an increase in foreign exchange that may be exported for travel purposes from the current 2,000 Ecu to 10,000.

--The International Monetary Fund has recommended the immediate taking of measures to change the job market in its preliminary report on the Greek economy handing to the government last week. THe IMF has said that the government, regardless of the outcome of social dialogue on the issue between the government, unions and employers, must make radical changes to the job market.

--Alpha Credit Bank's move last week to cut lending rates served to give Greece's largest commercial bank a larger share of the market held by state-run banks. Bankers in the state-run sector are expected to respond to the challenge this week, along with other major commercial banks. The sure winners in the battle for the hearts and pockets of clients is bound to be clients.

--This year will see the implementation of the government's first measures on changes to the job market, as well as a taste of the reforms to the social security system, including measures to cut back on evasion of pension contribution payments.

--As the Athens Stock Exchange general price index edges surely towards a new all-time high, increasing 30 percent since the sudden fall in March, the continuing interest rate cuts and increased capital inflows due to new ASE members have fanned hopes that the general price index can reach the benchmark of 2,000 points within the year.
